correctness.rationale: The logarithmic weights have ordered pairwise intersections T_i=(n-i)log R; at each such intersection every other weight and its first two scaled derivatives is O_n(R^-1) relative to the adjacent pair. The limiting two-rate beta is 1+s/(1+2s)^2, with a nondegenerate maximum 9/8 at s=1/2. C² convergence yields n−1 distinct local maxima with claimed locations and heights. Between them a single rate dominates so beta tends to one. Exact rational disjoint peak brackets for n=3 checked by the standalone program.

value.rationale: Local hydrological recession exponents are used to distinguish storage–discharge behavior. A single time-invariant sum of linear reservoirs can exhibit arbitrarily many well-separated apparent departures, each with the same order-one peak amplitude and intervening near-linear plateaus. The all-n construction, explicit scalings and rigorous local peak existence are nontrivial structural evidence of interpretation nonuniqueness, not merely a two-reservoir restatement.
